_about: The single source of truth for every input a reproducible Mini Xiangqi build consumes, per docs/engine-integration.md. The build verifies every hash before packaging and fails on a mismatch rather than shipping unverified bytes. The Fairy-Stockfish fork repository owns how its patches are implemented and how its own artifacts are built; this file records which revision and which inputs the app consumes, so that an app build is reproducible without reading the fork's history.
_field_names_are_provisional: docs/engine-integration.md leaves the manifest's concrete field names and schema version to be fixed when the first build consumes it. Nothing here has been consumed by a packaging build yet, so the names below are a proposal, not a frozen schema. Every value whose 'established' field is false is recorded as null or an empty list rather than as a plausible-looking placeholder; no hash in this file was invented. One field has been added under that licence rather than by fixing the schema: build_flags.platforms.windows.toolchain_core, because the compiler that builds the core and the stack that packages the frontend become known at different times on Windows, and one boolean over one 'toolchain' object cannot say that half of it is measured. manifest_version stays 1: nothing existing changed shape, and the reader in core/CMakeLists.txt asks for none of this.

fork._patches_about: The ordered list of focused changes present in the pinned revision, oldest first. docs/engine-integration.md accepts eight focused changes, and every one of them has landed: patches_pending is empty, so what the app consumes and what the contract requires are the same thing.

patches.summary: Adds the promotedSoldiersChaseable variant property so Mini Xiangqi soldiers, which are internally promoted from the start, are excluded as perpetual-chase targets. The property's default preserves every existing variant's adjudication.

Replaces the process exits on transposition-table allocation failure and on the Windows large-page free path, which the accepted error contract forbids. Until it lands, MXQ_ERR_ENGINE_HASH_ALLOCATION_FAILED is unreachable.
A static library target for every supported platform, which the core links. The fork's Makefile currently produces an executable and a Python module, neither of which the core can consume.
Corrects two defects that produce false terminal losses: a chaser counted as chasing while pinned, and a flying-general pin test that counts only the victim's own pieces on the shared file.
Completes the exclusion of generals and soldiers as chase targets in the discovered-check classifier path, so the exclusion holds in every path rather than in two of three.

Reports which rule produced an optional game end, through a read-only out-parameter on Position::is_optional_game_end and the OptionalGameEndRule enumeration. It changes no adjudication; it exposes one the engine already made. The core needs it because a neutral threefold and a mutual perpetual chase are the same draw value, and unlike mutual perpetual check a mutual chase leaves no trace in the move history to derive it from.

Corrects the repetition window's parity asymmetry, which evaluates one side over a wider span than the other and resolves a mutual perpetual chase as a unilateral loss. Lands with the fixture pinning that corner.

Gives search threads an explicit 8 MiB stack on MSVC, which fell through to std::thread and the Windows 1 MB default while Apple, MinGW and pthreads builds all took the 8 MiB path. Under LARGEBOARDS every MovePicker holds a 64 KB move array and search nests one per ply, so a deep search overflowed the 1 MB stack and killed the process.

static_library._note: The fork's static-library target landed at 86dad87e. The core does not consume the artifact: it compiles the copied source snapshot with a core-owned CMakeLists.txt, because the app needs arm64 and arm64e from one build system and the fork's Makefile is a second one. The target is what the contract requires of the fork; whether the core switches to consuming its artifact is a separate decision, and core/third_party/fairy-stockfish/README.md records what would change.
static_library.build_command: make lib ARCH=apple-silicon COMP=clang nnue=no largeboards=yes all=yes

vendored._about: How the pinned revision reaches the core: as a copied source snapshot compiled by a core-owned CMakeLists.txt, rather than as an artifact built by the fork. core/third_party/fairy-stockfish/README.md justifies the copied-snapshot choice against a submodule and a subtree, and records what would change if the core consumed the fork's own static-library target instead.
vendored._excluded_about: The engine's own main(), its Python bindings, its JavaScript/WebAssembly bindings, the fork's build system, and the fork's sample variant configuration. setup.py, pyffish.pyi, MANIFEST.in, tests/, .github/, appveyor.yml and test.py are outside source_paths and so are not present either.
vendored._hash_about: file_manifest lists the SHA-256 of every file in the snapshot, one per line, and file_manifest_sha256 is the SHA-256 of that listing. Verify the snapshot with 'shasum -a 256 -c ../SOURCES.sha256' from the snapshot directory. Both hashes were computed from the vendored bytes; neither is a placeholder.

build_flags._about: The build flags and defines the app build uses for each supported platform. No packaging build exists on any platform, so no flag set is established on any platform. The toolchain and architecture entries below are established — by docs/testing.md on the Apple platforms, and on Windows by the build recorded under windows.toolchain_core — and are recorded so that the unestablished parts are visibly the flags alone.
build_flags._core_build_note: The core's own CMake build of the vendored engine does compile it with a concrete define set, on macOS/arm64 and now on Windows/x64. That set is stated, and each entry cited back to a line of the fork's Makefile at the pinned revision, in core/third_party/fairy-stockfish/CMakeLists.txt — which is also where the one place the two platforms differ is written down: IS_64BIT reaches the compiler from the command line under Clang and from types.h under MSVC, so it is defined exactly once on each. It is deliberately not copied here: these fields describe the packaging build, which does not exist, and recording a developer build's flags under them would make an unestablished value look established. The sqlite_defines arrays are the one exception, filled on the Apple platforms while the platform entries stay unestablished: that set is hardening policy required by docs/game-data.md — identical on every platform and independent of any toolchain — decided and annotated in core/third_party/sqlite/CMakeLists.txt, which every build of the core applies. The Windows arrays stay empty with the rest of that unpinned entry.

windows._note: 'established' still reads false here for the same reason it does on the three Apple entries: it is about the packaging build these flag fields describe, and no Windows packaging build exists. What a real build did establish is under toolchain_core — measured on 2026-07-30 by the first build of the core on Windows that compiled the engine and passed every suite, in both the debug and the release configuration. The rest waits for the Windows frontend: the Windows App SDK and .NET versions have nothing to pin until a frontend uses them, and engine_flags and sqlite_flags belong to a packaging build, exactly as on the Apple platforms. sqlite_defines stays empty rather than copying the Apple list: that list is hardening policy every build of the core applies, so it would be true here, but this entry records what a Windows packaging build applied and no Windows packaging build has applied anything.
windows._toolchain_note: Deliberately still null. This field is the packaging toolchain — the Windows App SDK version, the .NET version, and what builds the WinUI 3 frontend — and naming the core's compiler here would make an unestablished value look established. toolchain_core below is the established part, kept in its own field rather than folded in.

toolchain_core._about: The core's Windows toolchain, pinned from the machine that built it rather than from intent. docs/engine-integration.md calls this manifest's field names provisional until a build consumes them; this field is new, and it is separate from 'toolchain' because the core's compiler and the frontend's packaging stack are established at different times and one being known says nothing about the other.

windows._architectures_note: x64 only. ARM64 came off the promised architectures on 2026-07-30 (owner decision) and returns when there is real hardware to test it on. Like deployment_target below, this is the product's target from docs/product.md rather than a measurement — it happens also to be the architecture the core-proof build produced, but it would read x64 either way, and when a packaging build first expresses it as a build setting this field takes that form.
windows._deployment_target_note: Windows 11 is the floor (owner decision, 2026-07-30): Windows 10 left Microsoft support in October 2025. The value is the product floor from docs/product.md, not a measurement — no packaging build has expressed it as a manifest or an SDK setting yet, and when one does this field takes that form.

variant._about: The bundled variant configuration. The identifier and the filename are fixed by docs/engine-integration.md. The file now exists, so its hash is computed from its bytes rather than left null. Editing the file changes this hash and must be done in the same change, or the packaging build fails rather than shipping unverified bytes.

network._about: The bundled NNUE network. The repository never contains these bytes in any form; they enter builds from a workspace- or CI-provided location. The filename must begin with the variant identifier, because the engine restricts NNUE to the matching variant by that basename prefix and a mismatch disables NNUE silently while the Use NNUE option still reads true. Only the filename differs from the source copy; the byte length and the SHA-256 are over content and are unchanged.
network._ci_delivery: How the bytes reach a CI runner, since they are in no repository and this one is public: from a location named by the MXQ_NNUE_URL repository secret, downloaded by .github/scripts/fetch-network.sh and verified by core/CMakeLists.txt against the byte_length and sha256 above before anything is staged. The location is deliberately not recorded here — a manifest pins content, and a URL is not content. Attaching the network to a release of this repository was considered and rejected: this repository is public, and docs/engine-integration.md makes establishing the network's origin and redistribution licence a mandatory gate for distribution beyond internal testing, which no one has passed. With no secret set the engine_search suite does not run in CI and the run says so; every other suite does.

sqlite._about: The vendored SQLite amalgamation, pinned to the newest stable release at core landing (3.53.4, released 2026-07-24, was the newest stable release on 2026-07-28 when the store landed). docs/game-data.md fixes a floor of 3.37.0 for STRICT tables, requires the hardened option set and no extension loading, and requires write-ahead logging with full synchronous durability and foreign keys on. The compile-time half of that hardening is the sqlite_defines list under build_flags, decided and annotated in core/third_party/sqlite/CMakeLists.txt; the connection-level half is applied and verified at open in core/src/mxq_store.cpp. sha256 was computed from the downloaded release archive's bytes; sha3_256_published is the checksum sqlite.org's download page lists for the same file, and the downloaded bytes match it.

vendored._about: How the pinned release reaches the core: as a verbatim copy of the amalgamation's library files, compiled by a core-owned CMakeLists.txt into mxq::sqlite, which mxq_core links PRIVATE. core/third_party/sqlite/README.md records the provenance, the public-domain license status, and why the archive's other two files are excluded.
vendored._excluded_about: The command-line shell's main() and the loadable-extension header; the build defines SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION, so the mechanism sqlite3ext.h exists for is exactly what is compiled out.
vendored._hash_about: file_manifest lists the SHA-256 of every file under upstream/, one per line, and file_manifest_sha256 is the SHA-256 of that listing. Verify with 'shasum -a 256 -c ../SOURCES.sha256' from the upstream directory. Both hashes were computed from the vendored bytes; neither is a placeholder.
